source: rules data (layout defaults): typical industry values, used only where no document gives one; every use is marked derived
height_tolerance_why: a documented AFF is a hard number: the box is set to it within a quarter inch

along_band_in.why: how far along the wall a box may drift from its drawn position to find a stud side (a switch stays by its door; a receptacle may move to the next stud)

faceplates_why: typical outer plate sizes by style (standard, mid-size, jumbo) and the added width per gang

box.why: a device box's width along the wall, one gang and each added gang

gang.why: devices this close side by side at one height share one plate

inside_cabinet_why: a box inside a cabinet is centred in it
casing_why: a door or window casing's width beside its opening: a plate must stay off it

default_heights_in.why: an object read without a height: its usual bottom and top above the floor (inches)

concealed.why: a refrigerator's receptacle is hidden behind it: the whole plate inside its back footprint on the wall, below its top, within the band of its centre line
a range's receptacle is behind the range, inside its footprint
a washer's or dryer's receptacle is behind the unit
a wall TV's receptacle and data outlet are behind the screen
a microwave's receptacle is inside its cabinet, centred
a dishwasher's (and disposal's) receptacle is in the sink base beside it, not behind the dishwasher
